newsitem.title: USA: FDIC's Helfer sees bank profits at $50 bln in '96.
newsitem.headline: FDIC's Helfer sees bank profits at $50 bln in '96.

text.p: Federal Deposit Insurance Corp Chairman Ricki Helfer said on Saturday that if bank earnings continued at the same pace as the first half of this year, industry profits could top $50 billion in 1996.

"If the commercial banking industry maintains the earnings strength it displayed during the first half of 1996, it will earn more than $50 billion in one year -- an annual record," Helfer told the American Bankers' Association convention.
The banking industry could see similar profitability in 1997, she said at a press briefing.

"If the economy remains strong I see no reason for there to be a significant change" in industry profitability next year, Helfer added. "Will it be as high as that ($50 billion), I don't know, but it could very well be in the ballpark."

Much depended on the durability of the economic expansion, Helfer said. "There are signs that the economy is slowing a bit, but that's viewed I think as more of a positive because of the inflation implications of that," she said.
The FDIC was "closely monitoring" the performance of bank credit card and other consumer loan portfolios because of a rise in credit card losses and personal bankruptcies, Helfer said.
At the moment regulators did not see any widespread risk to the banking system or significant problems for individual banks from those factors, she said.
"If the charge-off rate continues, and if the personal bankruptcy rate goes higher, then we may be more concerned. At the moment it's simply an area to watch and to monitor," Helfer said.
On Tuesday the FDIC board will consider a proposal to set a special assessment on thrifts following recent legislation to boost the under-capitalised Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF).
Under the new legislation, the savings and loan industry must provide about $4.5 billion to lift the SAIF, which insures deposits at thrifts, to the mandated level.
The FDIC staff has proposed that the one-time special assessment for thrifts be 65.7 cents per $100 of insured deposits, Helfer said.
The new law also requires banks for the first time to pay part of the annual interest payments on Financing Corp (FICO) bonds which were issued in the late 1980s for the savings and loan bailout.
FICO interest payments had been made solely from thrift premiums to the SAIF. That had been the main factor slowing the build-up of the thrift deposit insurance fund.
The FDIC board meeting to set new premiums for thrifts and banks in the aftermath of the legislation would probably be in November, Helfer said.
